newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus has no plans for film bidding war.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus has no plans for film bidding war.

text.p: Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure said on Tuesday that he had no plans to engage in a bidding war with rival TPS digital satellite television venture for obtaining the rights to broadcast films.

"The total amount that Canal Satellite will spend on foreign broadcast rights will not exceed the global amount that I have fixed and I can tell you that the total is of the same order that TPS is paying to Paramount alone," he told an industrial conference.
Patrick Le Lai, chairman of France's private broadcaster TF1, and major partner in TPS, on Monday said TPS had signed audiovisual rights deals with Hollywood studios MGM and Paramount.
TPS is a joint venture of TF1, state-owned France Television, M6, France Telecom and Lyonnaise des Eeaux.
Lescure said Canal Plus was in negotiations with many studios but had no intention of disclosing its partners.
"We will have those deals that TPS doesn't announce," he said.
